image.alt: Close view of Philodendron Birkin leaves, dark green with fine creamy pinstripes running out from the midrib

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but new leaves come back plainer

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones, out of direct sun

snap: A compact, self-heading Philodendron whose dark leaves carry fine creamy pinstripes running out from the midrib. New leaves open plain and draw their stripes as they expand. Bright filtered light is what keeps the pattern, and it is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Not a wild species but a sport that appeared in cultivation on a Philodendron 'Rojo Congo'. It is self-heading, holding a tidy upright clump rather than climbing, and grows slowly enough to keep a desk for years.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top inch of the mix has dried, in a loose, chunky aroid mix. It is a slow grower, so it wants less water and far less feeding than its leaf size suggests.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The pinstriping is unstable, and that is the thing worth knowing before buying. Every leaf is marked differently, the occasional one opens almost pure white, and a stem that reverts goes back to the deep red-green of the Rojo Congo it came from. Bright light keeps it striping; a dim corner sends it plain.
